html:
SMTO-SKL-0150 — Slack's sign-in reply was incomplete

GUID: 474aa8a0-bec5-5727-bd94-1ddb2fbad2ef
Slug: slack-token-response-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Slack's reply to SMTO's sign-in request was missing a usable sign-in or the list of permissions. This can happen when you first connect or when SMTO renews an older sign-in. Either way, Slack needs to be connected again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to connect Slack again using the same saved Slack app name, then open the new approval link it gives you. Each approval link works only once, so a fresh one is needed after a failed sign-in.
  2. In Slack, check that you're signing in to the right workspace, then approve the permissions shown. Slack sends the sign-in and permissions only after you approve in the intended workspace.
  3. If it fails again, ask the person who set up the Slack app to check its sign-in settings in Slack, especially any recent change to token expiry. An expiring sign-in that arrives without its renewal part is rejected by SMTO.

What success looks like

  • The Agent reports Slack as connected, and asking it for your Slack connection status shows it as connected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the Slack app. Don't paste Slack tokens, codes or the app's secret into the conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack token validation failed in the oauth.v2.access / oauth.v2.user.access response, during first connection or during automatic token rotation: missing or malformed access/refresh token, missing or malformed granted scope string, an invalid expires_in, expires_in without a refresh_token, or a non-object authed_user.

What this means

  • Token exchange fails bounded token/refresh/scope/expiry validation or the expected user token object is malformed. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Token exchange fails bounded token/refresh/scope/expiry validation or the expected user token object is malformed.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe token-schema failure details without displaying credentials.

How to fix it

  • token_bundle in skills/slack/oauth.py rejected the token response, either in SlackOAuth.complete (new consent; nothing is saved) or in SlackProvider.authorized during refresh (the record is left in reauthorization_required). Start slack.connect again with the same auth_app_ref and workspace_key; if it repeats, check the Slack app's OAuth and token rotation settings (an expiring token must come with a refresh token) and report the failing step with the error details.
  • Reconnect the exact Slack app; token responses must include valid tokens and actual granted scopes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported consent yields a valid bounded token bundle for the exact principal.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
